title: Ines and the Rivergate
premise: Orsen Ishikawa, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vane brothers' optimistic loan operation, takes a salvage job up the Rivergate to find a missing survey expedition. He discovers the expedition's survivors hiding in a flooded mining town, guarded by a girl named Ines who remembers everything the river has swallowed — including evidence that the Vanes engineered the expedition's disappearance to bury a land claim. Hunted by the Vanes' enforcers and the early snows, Orsen and Ines cross the range with the survivors, carrying proof that could ruin the Vanes. At the Rivergate's mouth, Orsen chooses justice over the debt forgiveness he's promised, exposing the brothers and gaining a family instead of freedom from his past.
about_author: Jonah Galloway is the pen name of a former river guide who spent a decade running freight through mountain waterways before turning to writing full-time. His fiction is known for weather that behaves like a character and endings that trade easy escapes for harder, warmer truths.

chapters.title: The Debt of Good Weather
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Chasing a supercell to film it, Orsen crashes his truck and learns the Vane brothers are calling his loan. The beat: charm masking dread, as he accepts a salvage job up the Rivergate to find a silent survey team — his last chance before winter collections begin.

chapters.title: Radio Silence at Mile Forty
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He hires a boat and pushes upriver, finding the expedition's abandoned camp: cold coffee, a smashed radio, drag marks leading into the timber. The beat: creeping wrongness as he realizes the silence wasn't an accident.

chapters.title: The Town That Floods on Purpose
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He reaches Harrowgate, a half-drowned mining town, and is ambushed by a girl with a slingshot and an unerring memory for terrain — Ines, who knows every path the water has erased. The beat: wary first alliance.

chapters.title: What Ines Remembers
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines shows Orsen the survivors — four expedition members hiding in the old church — and recites, from memory, the route the river took the night the expedition was attacked. The beat: awe at her mind, and the first hint the attack was human.

chapters.title: Ledger of a Drowned Claim
chapters.summary: Survivor Mara's POV. Mara reveals the expedition found mineral rights that would bankrupt the Vane brothers, and that their 'rescue' was an ambush. The beat: the mystery becomes a conspiracy, and the survivors become witnesses.

chapters.title: Smoke on the North Bank
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Enforcers torch a decoy camp; Orsen leads the group into the mine shafts to hide. The beat: claustrophobic fear, and Orsen realizing he can no longer pretend this is just a job.

chapters.title: Terms of Forgiveness
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Via radio, the Vanes offer to wipe Orsen's debt if he delivers Mara and the claim documents alone. The beat: temptation laid bare, and Orsen lying to the survivors that no offer was made.

chapters.title: Ines Sees the Lie
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines, who memorized the radio exchange, confronts Orsen privately but doesn't expose him — instead she asks what he wants to be when the river lets him go. The beat: shame, and the first crack in his self-interest.

chapters.title: The Range Ahead of the Snows
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The group sets out over the pass with five days before snow closes it. The beat: grim momentum, the wilderness indifferent to their justice.

chapters.title: Cold Camp at the Saddle
chapters.summary: Survivor Teo's POV. A storm strands them; Teo's frostbite worsens, and Ines navigates a whiteout by memory alone. The beat: the found family begins to cohere around Ines's gift.

chapters.title: The Bridge the River Ate
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The only crossing is a rotted trestle; Orsen rigs a line and nearly drowns saving Teo. The beat: sacrifice that costs him his salvage fee — the money that was supposed to save him.

chapters.title: Hunters on the Scree
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The Vanes' enforcers close in; the group splits to draw them off. The beat: terror and resolve, Orsen choosing the survivors over his escape route.

chapters.title: Ines's Country
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines leads them through a canyon only she can read, revealing her past: her father was a surveyor the Vanes ruined, and the river raised her. The beat: her grief becomes the group's compass.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They recover a cache — the original claim documents — hidden by Ines's father years ago. The beat: the past surfacing as ammunition; hope sharpening into a plan.

chapters.title: The Vane Brothers
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. Aldous and Merrick Vane argue over whether to kill Orsen or buy him; their optimism curdles into cruelty. The beat: the enemy humanized and made more frightening.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Narrows
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The enforcers trap the group; Ines floods a channel to scatter them, but Teo is taken. The beat: victory with a price, and Orsen's guilt over the lie resurfacing.

chapters.title: Confession at the Fire
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen tells the survivors about the Vanes' offer. Mara's forgiveness is conditional; Ines's is not. The beat: the emotional nadir and turning point — trust rebuilt by truth.

chapters.title: Trade at the Rivergate
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen walks alone into the Vanes' riverfront depot, offering himself and the documents — a ruse to draw the brothers from their guards. The beat: high tension, the con within the con.

chapters.title: The Water Rises
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines triggers the old floodgates, drowning the depot's escape routes as Mara's evidence reaches the arriving magistrate's launch. The beat: the wilderness itself delivering the justice the law was too slow to.

chapters.title: Ledgers Closed
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The Vanes are arrested; their debt to Orsen burns with their records. Orsen refuses the magistrate's reward, asking instead for the survivors' land claim to be honored. The beat: justice chosen over profit.

chapters.title: First Snow
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Snow falls on the pass as the group — now a household — settles into rebuilt Harrowgate. Orsen stays, repairing the church roof. The beat: quiet warmth, family chosen and kept.

chapters.title: The River Forgets Nothing
chapters.summary: Dual Orsen/Ines POV. A year later, Orsen chases storms again but always returns upriver; Ines teaches him the water's memory. The beat: resolution — the wilderness forgives nothing, but people can, and do.
